To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have prepared a small library of sugar modified nucleobase derivatives and we have investigated their ability to form G-quadruprelxes in solution, their ability to form organogels, their ability to transport ions across phospholipid membranes, and their cytotoxic activity against human MCF7 cancer cells.

a series of guanosine derivatives with sugar-modified side chains have been synthesized, showing a good ability to form G-quadruplices, to act as ionophores and to be low-molecular-weight gelling agents.
a small library of sugar-functionalized guanosine derivatives was synthesized and characterized.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design and synthesis of guanosine derivatives with a sugar moiety, and their biological evaluation.
the preparation of guanosine derivatives bearing a sugar moiety as a structural modification, and with the evaluation of their physico-chemical and biological properties.

the design and synthesis of guanosine derivatives with amphiphilic character, and the evaluation of their self-organising ability, their ability to form G-quadruprelxes, their activity in H(+) transportation through phospholipids and their cytotoxic profile.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

guanosine-based compounds, with the right structural features, may be used as promising candidates for the design of novel therapeutic agents, with the potential of acting in a variety of different ways.

the sugar-modified guanine derivatives reported herein may be considered as interesting and versatile molecular scaffolds for the design of bioactive compounds, and that their biological properties can be modulated by the introduction of suitable structural modifications.

the guanosine-based molecules here described are able to form G-quadrupleges in different organic solvents, and that their structural modifications may be exploited to obtain new materials with different biological and technological applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
, although the biological activities of the compounds herein reported are not yet fully characterised, the results obtained suggest a potential role of these compounds as drug candidates.

guanosine derivatives bearing sugar moieties, and particularly those bearing oligoethylene glycols and amino acids, are able to self-organise into supramolecular structures and to mediate ion transportation across phospholipid membranes.

the introduction of hydrophobic and hydrophilic chains, as well as charged groups, in guanosine-based systems may lead to a modulation of the biological properties of these nucleobases, with the potential to develop novel drug candidates.
The main takeaway from our work is that
guanosine derivatives, modified on the sugar moiety, can display different biological properties, including G-quadruplace formation, organogelation, ion transportation and cytotoxicity.
the sugar-modified guanine derivatives herein presented may be useful in the preparation of novel supramolecular systems, as well as for the development of new therapeutic agents.
the introduction of sugar residues into guanosine derivatives may lead to the design of new bioactive molecules.
